discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 190927
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
527 AM EDT Mon Oct 19 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry and pleasant weather persists through the entire week with
  highs either side of 70, lows in the 40s, and no rain in 
  sight.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 304 AM EDT Mon Oct 19 2026

Dew points were in the 20s and 30s this past weekend, but will be 
rising through the 40s today through Wednesday. This is as 
southwesterly flow Sunday and today promote moistening. Veering 
winds to easterly occurs Tuesday as a backdoor cold front approaches 
and washes out. As long as east winds continue Tuesday night/Wed AM 
and remain light, fog could occur as marine air is advected 
westward. A cold front approaches from the northwest Wednesday and 
may disrupt fog formation if clouds get to those areas early enough. 
This study of moisture content also begs the question about fire 
weather potential. Well, winds are expected to remain light enough 
to remove fire weather concern and limit that to grass fires at 
best. Given this mention of dry weather, rain chances will continue 
to be limited to less than wetting through most of Sunday. A cold 
front approaching late next weekend to early the following week (7-8 
days away) would be the next chance to see rain, but it's a small 
chance.

After starting this morning with a chance for frost, attention turns 
to tonight to see if we have another chance for frost. This is as 
long as the growing season remains intact. Given that dew points are 
expected to warm, low temps will have more of a floor to prevent 
cooling. Additionally, a cold front brings high clouds to the area 
Monday night limiting radiational cooling. Given these factors, have 
passed on issuing anything for frost Monday night. Lows stay more in 
the 40s for Tuesday night and beyond, meaning our next frost chance 
won't be for a while now.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 527 AM EDT Mon Oct 19 2026

VFR with mainly clear skies and light winds through the TAF
cycle and beyond.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...Frost Advisory until 9 AM EDT /8 AM CDT/ this morning for 
     INZ005>009-012>015-017-018-020-022>027-032>034-103-104-

OH...Frost Advisory until 9 AM EDT this morning for OHZ001-002-004-
     005-015-016-024-025.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

spc.text:
SPC AC 191629

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1129 AM CDT Mon Oct 19 2026

   Valid 191630Z - 201200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS SOUTHEAST
   ARIZONA/SOUTHWEST NEW MEXICO...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms may produce isolated marginally severe hail and gusty
   winds this afternoon and early evening across parts of southeast
   Arizona and southwest New Mexico.

   ...Southeast Arizona/southwest New Mexico...
   Generally cloud-free skies are noted late this morning as heating
   has steadily occurred in the presence of a relatively moist airmass
   with prevalent 50s F surface dewpoints in lower elevations.
   Satellite imagery/derived-winds continue to portray a 35-45 kt
   southwesterly mid-level jet associated with a weak shortwave trough
   will continue northeastward today. Modest large-scale ascent related
   to this feature coupled with terrain-driven influences should aid
   thunderstorm initiation across southeast Arizona this afternoon as
   convective temperatures are reached.

   The boundary layer will not become overly well mixed across this
   region through the afternoon, which should allow for around 500-1000
   J/kg of MLCAPE to develop. This instability coupled with cool
   mid-level temperatures and 30-40 kt of deep-layer shear appear
   sufficient for some updraft organization with the scattered to
   numerous thunderstorms that form. Isolated, marginally severe hail
   and gusty outflow winds may occur with the stronger cells that
   develop and spread east-northeastward across southeast Arizona into
   southwest New Mexico through the afternoon and early evening. This
   activity is expected to quickly weaken by mid-evening with the loss
   of daytime heating.

   ..Guyer/Mosier.. 10/19/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 190533

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1233 AM CDT Mon Oct 19 2026

   Valid 201200Z - 211200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are expected on Tuesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper trough will deepen along the West Coast on Tuesday,
   resulting in a broad low-level mass response with a return flow of
   low-level moisture across the Desert Southwest into the Great Basin
   and central High Plains regions. Deep-layer ascent associated with
   this broad axis of low-level moisture will result in at least widely
   scattered thunderstorm development through the day across the Great
   Basin into the Desert Southwest and High Plains. A couple instances
   of strong surface wind gusts may accompany thunderstorms in the
   Lower Colorado River Basin given stronger flow fields aloft. At the
   moment though, buoyancy appears too limited to support an organized
   severe gust threat, so severe probabilities have been withheld this
   outlook. By later Tuesday night, cooler mid-level temperatures
   associated with the upper trough will overspread a marine boundary
   layer along the CA coastline, promoting thunderstorm chances here as
   well.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/19/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 190652

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0152 AM CDT Mon Oct 19 2026

   Valid 211200Z - 221200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS
   OF CENTRAL AND EASTERN ARIZONA INTO FAR WESTERN NEW MEXICO...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated severe wind/hail and perhaps a brief tornado may occur over
   portions of Arizona into western New Mexico on Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper trough will continue to deepen while traversing the
   Interior West on Wednesday, provoking a strong low-level mass
   response across the Desert Southwest and Rockies into the High
   Plains. Adequate low-level moisture will stream northward across CA
   and the Interior West, beneath strong, nearly unidirectional
   southwesterly flow aloft. At least scattered thunderstorms are
   anticipated across much of the CONUS west of the Rockies. However,
   the richest low-level moisture and associated buoyancy will reside
   in the Lower Colorado River Basin, where an isolated severe threat
   will exist.

   ...Lower Colorado River Basin...
   Across the Lower Colorado River Basin, low to mid 50s F surface
   dewpoints will advect northward beneath 6.5+ C/km mid-level lapse
   rates and a 50-80 kt 500 mb jet streak. 500-1000 J/kg MLCAPE may
   manifest amid large and elongated hodographs. These conditions would
   support multicells and perhaps a few supercell structures with an
   attendant isolated severe wind/hail threat and perhaps a brief
   tornado, warranting the introduction of Category 1/Marginal Risk
   probabilities this outlook.

   ...Central California Valley Region...
   On Wednesday afternoon, a 70+ kt southerly 500 mb jet, as well as 7+
   C/km mid-level lapse rates, will overspread central and southern CA
   as the upper trough overspreads the San Joaquin Valley. The strong,
   nearly unidirectional flow will yield slightly curved, but very
   elongated hodographs. Such conditions would typically favor the
   development of low-topped supercells. However, surface
   temperatures/dewpoints in the upper 50s/mid 40s F may limit buoyancy
   considerably, precluding severe probabilities this outlook.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/19/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
